    {
      "option": "A",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "Suppose a farmer has four acres of land and he actually needs only two workers and himself to carry out various operations on his farm in a year, but if he employs five workers and his family members such as his wife and children, this situation is known as disguised unemployment.",
      "reason": "Directly aligns with NCERT illustration and definition of disguised unemployment."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Open unemployment, because the extra persons have no work at all and are seeking jobs",
      "premise_source": "stem",
      "evidence_id": "",

      "reason": "Workers are actively engaged on the farm rather than visibly without work."
    },
    {

      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Seasonal unemployment, because farm work is available only in some months of the year",

      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "carry out its operations through the year. He employs five workers along with his wife and children, and everyone on the farm works throughout the year.",

    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Full employment, because every person on the farm is working",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "Economists call unemployment prevailing in Indian farms as disguised unemployment.",
      "reason": "Excess labour on the farm represents disguised unemployment, not genuine full employment."
    }
